desc: Default token budget of nm_context_pack when a caller does not specify tokens (1,000 to 16,000 tokens).
help: Default token budget of nm_context_pack when a caller does not specify tokens (1,000 to 16,000 tokens).
label: Context pack token allowance

desc: Chunk tokens each tentacle window holds when composing its lens territory (2,000 to 32,000 tokens).
help: Chunk tokens each tentacle window holds when composing its lens territory (2,000 to 32,000 tokens).
label: Tentacle window token allowance

desc: Tokens of each candidate piece the judge reads around the question's evidence in full mode (128 to 2,048 tokens).
help: Tokens of each candidate piece the judge reads around the question's evidence in full mode (128 to 2,048 tokens).
label: Judge read window

desc: Top candidates from the stack that the reranker judges in fast mode (1 to 16 items).
help: Top candidates from the stack that the reranker judges in fast mode (1 to 16 items).
label: Fast mode candidate allowance

desc: Maximum wall-clock time allowance in seconds for a single forage or context pack run (5 to 180 seconds).
help: Maximum wall-clock time allowance in seconds for a single forage or context pack run (5 to 180 seconds).
label: Run time budget ceiling

desc: Device memory threshold in MiB above which homeostasis narrows neural ordering and suspends idle slots. Auto (default) follows this machine's card: its total memory less the live calls' measured room. A number pins it (1,024 MiB up to 80 GiB).
help: Device memory threshold in MiB above which homeostasis narrows neural ordering and suspends idle slots. Auto (default) follows this machine's card: its total memory less the live calls' measured room. A number pins it (1,024 MiB up to 80 GiB).
label: Graphics card memory ceiling

desc: On: when a caller omits an explicit token budget and the top reranked piece dominates with high confidence, the assembled pack is capped to the focused pack token allowance below instead of filling the full pack budget with lower-ranked tail pieces. Off: always fills up to the full context pack token allowance.
help: On: when a caller omits an explicit token budget and the top reranked piece dominates with high confidence, the assembled pack is capped to the focused pack token allowance below instead of filling the full pack budget with lower-ranked tail pieces. Off: always fills up to the full context pack token allowance.
label: Adaptive pack sizing

desc: Token ceiling applied when adaptive pack sizing detects a high-confidence focused answer (500 to 8,000 tokens).
help: Token ceiling applied when adaptive pack sizing detects a high-confidence focused answer (500 to 8,000 tokens).
label: Focused pack token allowance

desc: Mid-layer candidate pruning inside the batched Qwen3 Reranker pass (including close-call judge) when --rerank-drop is not set on the command line. Balanced (default): at layer 18, drops candidates trailing the leader by more than 4.0 log-odds while keeping at least the top 5 through all layers. Aggressive: layer 16, margin 3.0, keep 3. Off: every candidate runs all layers.
help: Mid-layer candidate pruning inside the batched Qwen3 Reranker pass (including close-call judge) when --rerank-drop is not set on the command line. Balanced (default): at layer 18, drops candidates trailing the leader by more than 4.0 log-odds while keeping at least the top 5 through all layers. Aggressive: layer 16, margin 3.0, keep 3. Off: every candidate runs all layers.
label: Reranker early candidate drop

desc: On (default): when the server is quiet and memory allows, Qwen3 1.7B (writer-base@3, ~1,087 MiB alongside the other three MicroModels within 2.17 GiB on a 4 GB card) summarizes served and contested pieces at idle, yielding immediately when a new request arrives or the server exits. Off: disables background writer notes.
help: On (default): when the server is quiet and memory allows, Qwen3 1.7B (writer-base@3, ~1,087 MiB alongside the other three MicroModels within 2.17 GiB on a 4 GB card) summarizes served and contested pieces at idle, yielding immediately when a new request arrives or the server exits. Off: disables background writer notes.
label: Idle writer notes

desc: Cumulative token allowance for context packs served in one session (0 for unlimited, up to 500,000 tokens). At 80% of an active quota the Nano automatically scales packs down to the focused allowance; at 100% it applies the quota action below.
help: Cumulative token allowance for context packs served in one session (0 for unlimited, up to 500,000 tokens). At 80% of an active quota the Nano automatically scales packs down to the focused allowance; at 100% it applies the quota action below.
label: Session context token quota

desc: Cumulative 24-hour token allowance across served context packs (0 for unlimited, up to 2,000,000 tokens). At 80% of an active quota packs scale down to the focused allowance; at 100% the quota action below applies.
help: Cumulative 24-hour token allowance across served context packs (0 for unlimited, up to 2,000,000 tokens). At 80% of an active quota packs scale down to the focused allowance; at 100% the quota action below applies.
label: Daily context token quota

desc: Maximum number of context pack calls served in one session before applying the quota action below (0 for unlimited, up to 500 packs).
help: Maximum number of context pack calls served in one session before applying the quota action below (0 for unlimited, up to 500 packs).
label: Session context pack call quota

desc: How the Nano responds when a session or daily quota is reached. Compact: scales each pack down to a compact focused budget so top citations still arrive with minimal token cost. Fast: also switches to fast mode (top stack candidates only). Withhold: withholds uncached packs with a quota notice until the quota is raised or reset to 0.
help: How the Nano responds when a session or daily quota is reached. Compact: scales each pack down to a compact focused budget so top citations still arrive with minimal token cost. Fast: also switches to fast mode (top stack candidates only). Withhold: withholds uncached packs with a quota notice until the quota is raised or reset to 0.
label: When a quota is reached

desc: Off: nothing recalled and nothing written to memory.
help: Off: nothing recalled and nothing written to memory.
label: Memory

desc: On: the vectors of the meaning index (one per piece of your material: a content hash and 1,024 numbers, never its text or file names) are kept in the project's memory folder, in dense/vectors.bin, so a restart does not embed everything again. Off: they are neither read nor written and nothing is deleted. With memory off nothing is kept. To clear it: neuromorph-nano dense clear --project <repo>, or POST /api/dense/clear; the next start embeds again.
help: On: the vectors of the meaning index (one per piece of your material: a content hash and 1,024 numbers, never its text or file names) are kept in the project's memory folder, in dense/vectors.bin, so a restart does not embed everything again. Off: they are neither read nor written and nothing is deleted. With memory off nothing is kept. To clear it: neuromorph-nano dense clear --project <repo>, or POST /api/dense/clear; the next start embeds again.
label: Keep the meaning index on disk

desc: On: the episode query vectors, decoy calibration floors and reranker pair scores of recall by meaning (content hashes, vectors and numbers only, never prompt or file text) are kept in the project's memory folder under meaning/, so a restart does not re-run the 28-layer decoy calibration. Off: kept in RAM only for the current process.
help: On: the episode query vectors, decoy calibration floors and reranker pair scores of recall by meaning (content hashes, vectors and numbers only, never prompt or file text) are kept in the project's memory folder under meaning/, so a restart does not re-run the 28-layer decoy calibration. Off: kept in RAM only for the current process.
label: Keep the recall meaning cache on disk

desc: On (default): G3 captures repeating positive decision patterns into the separate muscle memory store (never touching base cartridges) and runs bounded idle replays to promote proven behavior packs. Off: disables G3 and muscle memory on serve.
help: On (default): G3 captures repeating positive decision patterns into the separate muscle memory store (never touching base cartridges) and runs bounded idle replays to promote proven behavior packs. Off: disables G3 and muscle memory on serve.
label: Muscle memory (G3)

desc: On: the 3-level Continuous Learning Engine and Supervisor (Level 1 Experiential, Level 2 Knowledge, Level 3 Behavioral) captures outcomes, corrections and preferences, extracts patterns and procedures, adapts retrieval and context allocation, and updates the 6 continual learning cartridges under regression supervision. Off: no continual learning observations or adaptations run.
help: On: the 3-level Continuous Learning Engine and Supervisor (Level 1 Experiential, Level 2 Knowledge, Level 3 Behavioral) captures outcomes, corrections and preferences, extracts patterns and procedures, adapts retrieval and context allocation, and updates the 6 continual learning cartridges under regression supervision. Off: no continual learning observations or adaptations run.
label: Continuous learning

desc: Auto: runs Cycle A (immediate experience and feedback capture) on every outcome and triggers Cycle B (pattern extraction, 5-category memory consolidation, policy generation, and supervisor validation) automatically when new evidence arrives. Immediate: runs Cycle A live and waits for a manual Cycle B trigger. Manual: consolidates only when triggered from the Learning page.
help: Auto: runs Cycle A (immediate experience and feedback capture) on every outcome and triggers Cycle B (pattern extraction, 5-category memory consolidation, policy generation, and supervisor validation) automatically when new evidence arrives. Immediate: runs Cycle A live and waits for a manual Cycle B trigger. Manual: consolidates only when triggered from the Learning page.
label: Continuous learning cycle

desc: Full: the whole path (reranker over more candidates, the code around the first place, callers, a second look). Fast: seconds, the reranker on the first few. A call can ask for either; applies when the server runs the whole path.
help: Full: the whole path (reranker over more candidates, the code around the first place, callers, a second look). Fast: seconds, the reranker on the first few. A call can ask for either; applies when the server runs the whole path.
label: Answer mode

desc: Full: advertises up to the configured MCP tool count below (default all 19 tools) in tools/list. Lean: caps tools/list to the 5 core coding tools (nm_context_pack, nm_symbol_find, nm_view, nm_deps, nm_feedback) to cut fixed MCP schema token overhead by ~74% per turn, while keeping all 19 tools callable by name in tools/call.
help: Full: advertises up to the configured MCP tool count below (default all 19 tools) in tools/list. Lean: caps tools/list to the 5 core coding tools (nm_context_pack, nm_symbol_find, nm_view, nm_deps, nm_feedback) to cut fixed MCP schema token overhead by ~74% per turn, while keeping all 19 tools callable by name in tools/call.
label: MCP tool exposure profile

desc: Exact number of Neuromorph Nano tools advertised in tools/list in coding priority order (1 for nm_context_pack only, 5 for the core coding set, 8 with repo map and build tools, up to all 25 tools; 19 by default, the 6 after them being the interface tools). Every tool remains callable by name in tools/call regardless of this count.
help: Exact number of Neuromorph Nano tools advertised in tools/list in coding priority order (1 for nm_context_pack only, 5 for the core coding set, 8 with repo map and build tools, up to all 25 tools; 19 by default, the 6 after them being the interface tools). Every tool remains callable by name in tools/call regardless of this count.
label: MCP advertised tool count

desc: Off: uses default model and server tool settings (all 19 tools unless dynamic lean mode is on). On: lets you select individually which of the 19 MCP tools you want to use; when Dynamic tool activation is off, unselected tools are hidden from tools/list and blocked from running.
help: Off: uses default model and server tool settings (all 19 tools unless dynamic lean mode is on). On: lets you select individually which of the 19 MCP tools you want to use; when Dynamic tool activation is off, unselected tools are hidden from tools/list and blocked from running.
label: MCP tool control

desc: Active when MCP tool control is On. Comma-separated list of the exact MCP tools you selected to keep ON (for example nm_context_pack,nm_symbol_find,nm_view,nm_build_run). With Dynamic tool activation Off, only these tools are advertised and allowed to run; with Dynamic On, these are your starting tools and additional tools can activate dynamically on demand.
help: Active when MCP tool control is On. Comma-separated list of the exact MCP tools you selected to keep ON (for example nm_context_pack,nm_symbol_find,nm_view,nm_build_run). With Dynamic tool activation Off, only these tools are advertised and allowed to run; with Dynamic On, these are your starting tools and additional tools can activate dynamically on demand.
label: Selected MCP tools

desc: On: dynamically activates additional MCP tools into tools/list (emitting notifications/tools/list_changed) on demand when the task or agent needs them, starting from either your Tool Control selection (when Tool Control is On) or the lean tool count (when Tool Control is Off). Off: keeps tools strictly fixed (all 19 defaults when Tool Control is Off, or strictly your selected tools when Tool Control is On).
help: On: dynamically activates additional MCP tools into tools/list (emitting notifications/tools/list_changed) on demand when the task or agent needs them, starting from either your Tool Control selection (when Tool Control is On) or the lean tool count (when Tool Control is Off). Off: keeps tools strictly fixed (all 19 defaults when Tool Control is Off, or strictly your selected tools when Tool Control is On).
label: Dynamic MCP tool activation

desc: On: setup writes "enableArtifact": false into the project's .claude/settings.local.json (or when setup --lean is passed), omitting Claude Code's large built-in Artifact tool description in interactive sessions to save prompt tokens and quota. Off: leaves Claude Code's built-in Artifact setting untouched.
help: On: setup writes "enableArtifact": false into the project's .claude/settings.local.json (or when setup --lean is passed), omitting Claude Code's large built-in Artifact tool description in interactive sessions to save prompt tokens and quota. Off: leaves Claude Code's built-in Artifact setting untouched.
label: Claude Code lean host settings

applies: next start of the interface server (switching off applies at once)
desc: Off: this computer only. View: paired tablets on your local network can read everything and change nothing. Control: they can also change settings. There is no encryption on the wire: anyone who can listen on your local network can read the traffic, including a tablet's token. Pair a tablet with the six-digit code (neuromorph-nano pair).
help: Off: this computer only. View: paired tablets on your local network can read everything and change nothing. Control: they can also change settings. There is no encryption on the wire: anyone who can listen on your local network can read the traffic, including a tablet's token. Pair a tablet with the six-digit code (neuromorph-nano pair).
label: Tablets on the local network

desc: Keep: the text of your prompts to Claude Code, seen through its hooks, is kept on this computer in the project's memory folder (prompts.jsonl), with anything that looks like a secret dropped first, for the days set below. Off: only each prompt's length and a hash are kept. Clear it with neuromorph-nano situation --project <repo> --clear-prompts.
help: Keep: the text of your prompts to Claude Code, seen through its hooks, is kept on this computer in the project's memory folder (prompts.jsonl), with anything that looks like a secret dropped first, for the days set below. Off: only each prompt's length and a hash are kept. Clear it with neuromorph-nano situation --project <repo> --clear-prompts.
label: Keep prompt text

desc: Primes: short notes the Nano adds to Claude Code's context through its hooks, unasked, when they are likely to help: at a prompt, the places that answered a similar verified question before; after a failed build or test, the change that fixed the same failure last time; before an edit, a verified fix in those lines or the callers of a changed signature; after the conversation is compacted, what was in play. Each cites its source, which is read fresh first; the same note is never given twice in a session. Quiet: only from strong evidence. On: also from weaker evidence, at a session start (what the last session left open) and at a stop with changes not built or tested. No count per session: each note is given only when its rule fires, and never twice. Off: none.
help: Primes: short notes the Nano adds to Claude Code's context through its hooks, unasked, when they are likely to help: at a prompt, the places that answered a similar verified question before; after a failed build or test, the change that fixed the same failure last time; before an edit, a verified fix in those lines or the callers of a changed signature; after the conversation is compacted, what was in play. Each cites its source, which is read fresh first; the same note is never given twice in a session. Quiet: only from strong evidence. On: also from weaker evidence, at a session start (what the last session left open) and at a stop with changes not built or tested. No count per session: each note is given only when its rule fires, and never twice. Off: none.
label: Priming

desc: What the Nano keeps, on this computer in the project's memory folder (training/), for fitting cartridges later from your verified work. Features: for each served context pack, every candidate it judged (place, a hash of its lines, its score from the reranker, whether it was served), what followed (used, verified, refuted, passed over, where Claude Code went instead), the settings, cartridges and hardware in use; preference signals (edits kept or reverted, corrections, stated rules, refusals) without text; timings per hardware piece. No question or passage text. Full: also the question and each judged passage's text, with anything that looks like a secret dropped, so examples stay usable after the code changes. Off: nothing. Nothing is kept with memory off. Clear it with neuromorph-nano examples --project <repo> --clear.
help: What the Nano keeps, on this computer in the project's memory folder (training/), for fitting cartridges later from your verified work. Features: for each served context pack, every candidate it judged (place, a hash of its lines, its score from the reranker, whether it was served), what followed (used, verified, refuted, passed over, where Claude Code went instead), the settings, cartridges and hardware in use; preference signals (edits kept or reverted, corrections, stated rules, refusals) without text; timings per hardware piece. No question or passage text. Full: also the question and each judged passage's text, with anything that looks like a secret dropped, so examples stay usable after the code changes. Off: nothing. Nothing is kept with memory off. Clear it with neuromorph-nano examples --project <repo> --clear.
label: Keep training examples

desc: Kept prompt text older than this is removed at the next read of the situation record, and at a prompt when the last removal was more than an hour ago (1 to 3,650 days).
help: Kept prompt text older than this is removed at the next read of the situation record, and at a prompt when the last removal was more than an hour ago (1 to 3,650 days).
label: Keep prompt text for (days)

desc: Free space the Nano keeps on the drive holding its folder: below it a job-filter build refuses to start and the storage view warns (1 to 1,000 GB). Prune rebuildable storage to free space.
help: Free space the Nano keeps on the drive holding its folder: below it a job-filter build refuses to start and the storage view warns (1 to 1,000 GB). Prune rebuildable storage to free space.
label: Disk floor (GB)

desc: The most card memory the Nano itself keeps: its MicroModels, window copies and working buffers. Under a limit it tiles batches smaller and evicts idle MicroModels (restoring them when needed) to stay within it. Auto (default) uses what the driver reports free. 0 runs every MicroModel on the processor from the next start. Applies live, with no restart (0 at the next start).
help: The most card memory the Nano itself keeps: its MicroModels, window copies and working buffers. Under a limit it tiles batches smaller and evicts idle MicroModels (restoring them when needed) to stay within it. Auto (default) uses what the driver reports free. 0 runs every MicroModel on the processor from the next start. Applies live, with no restart (0 at the next start).
label: Graphics card memory limit (MiB)

desc: The most host memory the Nano plans for: the kept encoded-chunk cache takes at most half of it, and the idle writer loads only when the limit less the Nano's own memory leaves it room. Auto (default) follows the memory available now. Applies live, with no restart.
help: The most host memory the Nano plans for: the kept encoded-chunk cache takes at most half of it, and the idle writer loads only when the limit less the Nano's own memory leaves it room. Auto (default) follows the memory available now. Applies live, with no restart.
label: System memory limit (MiB)

desc: The most processor threads the Nano's work runs on at once (questions and background indexing and writing), so the machine stays responsive. Auto (default) uses every thread; background work still yields to a question. Applies live, at the next stage.
help: The most processor threads the Nano's work runs on at once (questions and background indexing and writing), so the machine stays responsive. Auto (default) uses every thread; background work still yields to a question. Applies live, at the next stage.
label: Processor threads limit
